title: The Testimony Of The Heavens 1st Degree The Heavens As The Page Of Divine Unity

questions.question: What is the title of the passage?
questions.answer: The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: Who is doing the observing and asking questions in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who is trying to learn about his Maker by looking at the universe.

questions.question: What does the opening line in Arabic and English tell us before the passage begins?
questions.answer: It begins in the name of Allah, showing that the discussion starts by remembering Him.

questions.question: According to the Qur’anic verse in the passage, which parts of creation praise Allah?
questions.answer: The heavens, the earth, and everything in them praise Allah.

questions.question: What does the verse say people do not understand well?
questions.answer: People do not understand how the created things glorify Allah.

questions.question: Which part of creation does the passage choose to talk about first?
questions.answer: It starts with the heavens.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with the heavens?
questions.answer: Because the heavens are always seen by people and they clearly point to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How is the world described for the traveler? Give one description.
questions.answer: It is described like a generous place of welcome, a place of learning, or a wonderful place to look at.

questions.question: What two big questions does the traveler ask when he enters the world?
questions.answer: He asks who made this world and who rules it.

questions.question: What does the face of the heavens seem to say to the traveler?
questions.answer: It invites him to look carefully so he can be guided to what he is searching for.

questions.question: What amazing thing does the traveler notice about the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: He sees huge bodies held up with no pillars or supports.

questions.question: How do the heavenly bodies move?
questions.answer: They move quickly and together in order without crashing into one another.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the lights in the sky?
questions.answer: They keep shining without needing fuel like oil.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the way everything in the sky is managed?
questions.answer: It is all managed at the same time in a perfect and balanced way, without any lack.

questions.question: How are the strong powers in the heavenly bodies described?
questions.answer: They are made obedient to a law.

questions.question: What happens to the face of the heavens besides being arranged?
questions.answer: It is kept clean and cleared of waste.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the movement of heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: They are compared to a disciplined army doing maneuvers.

questions.question: What does the turning of the earth show people?
questions.answer: It shows the heavens in changing scenes every night and every year, like pictures being displayed.

questions.question: What main idea about the heavens is the traveler meant to understand?
questions.answer: The heavens are carefully controlled and ordered, and this points to Allah’s power and rule.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the passage?
questions.answer: It is about a traveler learning about Allah by observing the universe.

questions.question: What does the Qur’anic verse teach about all created things?
questions.answer: They all praise and glorify Allah.

questions.question: What important limit does the verse place on human understanding?
questions.answer: Humans do not fully grasp the way creation praises Allah.

questions.question: Why are the heavens a strong place to begin this search?
questions.answer: They are open for everyone to see and they fill people with wonder.

questions.question: What does the traveler think the world is like?
questions.answer: He sees it as a welcoming, well-prepared, meaningful place.

questions.question: What does the traveler want to know about this world?
questions.answer: He wants to know its maker and ruler.

questions.question: What appears before the traveler first?
questions.answer: The beautiful sky filled with stars.

questions.question: What effect do the stars have on the traveler?
questions.answer: They draw his attention and guide him to think about the One who made them.

questions.question: What does the traveler see happening in the heavens?
questions.answer: He sees a ruling power carrying out many tasks.

questions.question: Why is it surprising that the heavenly bodies stay where they are?
questions.answer: Because they are extremely heavy, yet they remain raised up without visible supports.

questions.question: Why is their movement also surprising?
questions.answer: Because they move very fast and still do not hit each other.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the sun and moon?
questions.answer: They each do their own work and do not go against their assigned duty.

questions.question: What does the phrase about managing everything “at the same time” show?
questions.answer: It shows great power, perfect control, and no weakness in ruling creation.

questions.question: What does cleaning the heavens suggest about the way the universe is run?
questions.answer: It suggests care, order, and purity rather than mess and confusion.

questions.question: Why are the heavenly bodies compared to an army?
questions.answer: Because they move in a controlled, organized, and obedient way.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the sky’s changing appearance?
questions.answer: It is compared to a screen showing different scenes.

questions.question: What feeling is the passage trying to build in the reader through these examples?
questions.answer: Wonder at the order and greatness of Allah’s creation.

questions.question: What conclusion can a student make from all these signs in the sky?
questions.answer: The sky is not random; it is directed with wisdom and purpose.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage faith?
questions.answer: It tells us to observe creation carefully and see Allah’s signs in it.

questions.question: In simple words, what is “The Supreme Sign” about?
questions.answer: It is about finding proof of Allah by looking at the universe.

questions.question: What kind of person is the traveler in the passage?
questions.answer: He is a thoughtful person who asks deep questions.

questions.question: What does the Qur’anic verse say about the seven heavens and the earth?
questions.answer: It says they glorify Allah.

questions.question: What else, besides the heavens and earth, glorifies Allah in the verse?
questions.answer: Everything that exists does.

questions.question: What are people unable to fully understand in that verse?
questions.answer: The way creation praises Allah.

questions.question: Where does the passage say we should begin looking for signs?
questions.answer: With the heavens.

questions.question: How is the world described as a place for people?
questions.answer: As a place of kindness, wisdom, beauty, and learning.

questions.question: What does the traveler ask about the world as if it were a book?
questions.answer: He asks who wrote it.

questions.question: What does the traveler ask about the world as if it were a kingdom?
questions.answer: He asks who its ruler is.

questions.question: What invites the traveler to think more deeply?
questions.answer: The sky full of stars.

questions.question: What is one sign of order in the heavens mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Huge heavenly bodies move together without crashing.

questions.question: What is one sign of power mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Massive bodies are kept up without pillars.

questions.question: What is one sign of steadiness mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The shining bodies continue their work without disorder.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by saying the sun and moon are put to work?
questions.answer: That they act according to a command and purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying all things are managed in the same way and with the same strength?
questions.answer: That one powerful ruler controls them all.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that the heavens are cleaned?
questions.answer: To show that even very large things are kept in order and neatness.

questions.question: What happens because the earth turns?
questions.answer: People see different views of the heavens over time.

questions.question: What lesson should a Muslim student take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should reflect on creation and let it lead us to know Allah better.

questions.question: What is the first name given to this section of the text?
questions.answer: The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What is the traveler questioning the universe about?
questions.answer: He is asking about his Maker.

questions.question: What does starting with the name of Allah teach the reader?
questions.answer: It teaches the reader to begin important matters by remembering Allah.

questions.question: What does the verse show about the job of creation?
questions.answer: Creation praises Allah.

questions.question: What does the verse show about people’s knowledge?
questions.answer: Our knowledge is limited because we do not fully understand that praise.

questions.question: What special place do the heavens have in this passage?
questions.answer: They are the first great sign the traveler studies.

questions.question: What is one reason the heavens are important signs for all people?
questions.answer: Everyone can look at them with amazement.

questions.question: How does the traveler view the world at first?
questions.answer: As a rich, carefully prepared place with many benefits and meanings.

questions.question: What are the traveler’s two main questions about this world?
questions.answer: Who made it and who governs it.

questions.question: What part of the sky catches his attention first?
questions.answer: The star-filled face of the heavens.

questions.question: What does the sky seem to offer the traveler?
questions.answer: Guidance toward the answer he is seeking.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn from the size and speed of the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: That something very powerful and wise is controlling them.

questions.question: Why is the lack of collisions important in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows careful order, not chaos.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying heavenly lamps burn without oil?
questions.answer: Their light continues in a way beyond ordinary human means.

questions.question: What does the management of everything in vast space show?
questions.answer: It shows complete control over a huge creation.

questions.question: What does obedience to law in the heavens tell us?
questions.answer: The heavens follow a set command and do not act on their own.

questions.question: Why is the army example a helpful comparison?
questions.answer: It helps us picture discipline, unity, and command.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the changing sky that people see?
questions.answer: Like scenes being shown to the audience of creation.

questions.question: What overall message does the traveler receive from the heavens?
questions.answer: They point him toward the greatness and control of Allah.

questions.question: What does the subtitle tell us the traveler is doing?
questions.answer: He is examining the universe to learn about his Maker.

questions.question: What is the meaning of beginning with “In the Name of Allah”?
questions.answer: It means starting with Allah’s help and remembrance.

questions.question: According to the verse, is praise of Allah limited to living things only?
questions.answer: No. Everything praises Allah.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that people do not grasp this praise?
questions.answer: There are realities in creation that are true even when we do not fully understand them.

questions.question: Why does the passage focus on the heavens before other things?
questions.answer: Because they are a clear and wonderful sign seen by everyone.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about the world that makes him ask questions?
questions.answer: He sees that it is beautiful, useful, and wisely arranged.

questions.question: Why would the traveler compare the world to a book?
questions.answer: Because it seems made with meaning, like something written by an author.

questions.question: Why would he compare it to a kingdom?
questions.answer: Because it appears to be ruled and organized.

questions.question: What in the heavens seems to call the traveler to investigate?
questions.answer: The shining sky filled with stars.

questions.question: What does the traveler discover in the heavens besides beauty?
questions.answer: He discovers action, order, and control.

questions.question: What is unusual about the heavenly bodies being held up?
questions.answer: They remain in place without visible supports.

questions.question: What is unusual about their motion?
questions.answer: They move very fast while staying in harmony.

questions.question: What does the passage show by mentioning that the lights keep burning without fuel?
questions.answer: Their working does not depend on ordinary human methods.

questions.question: What do the words about no disturbance or disorder teach?
questions.answer: The universe is run in a stable and careful way.

questions.question: What is learned from the sun and moon each having their own tasks?
questions.answer: They are given duties and follow them.

questions.question: What does ruling over unmeasurable space without deficiency tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us the ruler has unlimited ability compared to creation.

questions.question: What does cleansing the heavens add to the picture of the universe?
questions.answer: It shows that the universe is not only powerful but also orderly and maintained.

questions.question: What does the cinema-like example help readers imagine?
questions.answer: The sky’s scenes changing again and again for people to observe.

questions.question: If a student summed up this passage in one sentence, what could he or she say?
questions.answer: The heavens are full of signs showing wise and powerful control by Allah.

questions.question: What is the central question of the traveler in this passage?
questions.answer: He wants to know who his Maker is.

questions.question: What does the Qur’anic verse say all things do for Allah?
questions.answer: They glorify and praise Him.

questions.question: What does the verse teach us about our own understanding?
questions.answer: We do not fully understand the praise made by creation.

questions.question: Which created thing is discussed first to help answer the traveler’s question?
questions.answer: The heavens.

questions.question: Why are the heavens a good first sign for this discussion?
questions.answer: They are visible to all people and inspire wonder.

questions.question: How does the traveler describe the world in a positive way?
questions.answer: As a generous, skillfully prepared, and meaningful place.

questions.question: What question does the traveler ask about the world as a “book”?
questions.answer: He asks who made it.

questions.question: What question does he ask about the world as a “realm”?
questions.answer: He asks who its king is.

questions.question: What seems to speak to the traveler first?
questions.answer: The starry heavens.

questions.question: What invitation does the sky give him?
questions.answer: To look carefully so he can find the answer he seeks.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about the number and size of heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: There are very many of them, and some are much larger than the earth.

questions.question: What does their speed show when they still stay in order?
questions.answer: It shows strong and precise control.

questions.question: Why is it important that they do not collide?
questions.answer: It proves there is harmony and planning in their movement.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the shining bodies and fuel?
questions.answer: They keep shining without needing fuel.

questions.question: What does the passage say about managing all things in endless space?
questions.answer: Everything is managed together with equal power and without any shortcoming.

questions.question: What happens to the violent or forceful powers in those bodies?
questions.answer: They are made obedient to a law.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give when speaking of cleaning the heavens?
questions.answer: It gives the picture of removing waste from a huge gathering place.

questions.question: What two comparisons are used near the end of the passage for the moving heavens?
questions.answer: A disciplined army and a screen showing scenes.

questions.question: What conclusion is the traveler meant to reach from all these observations?
questions.answer: The heavens are under the control of a wise and mighty Creator, Allah.
